children: T-Mobile
raised its full-year free cash flow outlook after delivering another strong quarter driven by postpaid account growth, higher average revenue per account and expanding margins.
The wireless carrier now expects
2026 service revenue of about $76.8 billion
and adjusted free cash flow of
$18.7 billion to $18.8 billion
, up from its previous outlook. Core adjusted EBITDA is now projected between $37.35 billion and $37.45 billion.
The company also increased its full-year postpaid ARPA growth forecast to about
, up from a previous range of 2.5% to 3%.
T-Mobile added
274,000 postpaid net accounts
during the third quarter while postpaid ARPA increased more than 4% year over year.
Postpaid service revenue rose 9%, total service revenue increased 6% and core adjusted EBITDA climbed 11%. Adjusted free cash flow margin reached
Digital engagement is also becoming a bigger part of the business.
T-Mobile's T-Life app now has
32 million monthly active users
, while more than 80% of upgrades and half of phone-line activations were completed digitally during Q3.
The company is also pushing deeper into AI-powered networking.
T-Mobile completed what management called the world's first
AI-RAN call
and announced a partnership with Amazon Web Services to build the first instances of its Kinetic Edge platform.
Not everything is moving in the same direction.
Management said stronger postpaid performance is being partially offset by the faster roll-off of the Boost MVNO business and continued weakness in prepaid.
Investor Takeaway
I think the strongest part of T-Mobile's quarter is that the company is showing
both volume and pricing power at the same time
It is adding postpaid accounts while ARPA is moving higher, which is a much healthier setup than relying purely on promotions to drive subscriber growth.
The higher free cash flow outlook also gives T-Mobile more flexibility around buybacks and future spectrum spending. Management said it has already completed
$10.3 billion of buybacks this year
, although more capital may be reserved for spectrum auctions in 2027 and 2028.
The risks are mainly around churn, prepaid weakness and whether promotional intensity rises in Q4.
For investors, the key things to watch are
postpaid ARPA, account growth, churn, FWA momentum, spectrum spending and whether digital efficiencies continue supporting margins
T-Mobile is still growing.
More importantly, it is generating more cash while doing it.

title: T-Mobile Delivers Major Surprise for Stock Investors
